NAME OF COLLECTING AGENT: Position, APPLICATION FOR ENROLLMENT IN A NONRESERVATION SCHOOL. (For a child not enrolled at an Agency.) For and in consideration of the United States assuming the care, education, and maintenance in the United States Indian School at Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wash., of Lizzie Brown female, I, Representative of the Parents of Ketchikan P. O., State of Alaska, do hereby voluntarily consent and agree to enrollment in said school for a period of years, and also obligate and bind myself to abide by all the rules and regulations for Indian schools. I further say that the said child was born at Ketchikan, Alaska on Oct. 10, 1901; that the father, Joe Brown, is Indian of the Klinket Tribe located at Agency; that he left the tribe about ; that the mother, Mrs. Emma Brown, is Indian of the Klinket Tribe located at Agency, and left the tribe about that the said child was born and reared in the United States, and now actually resides therein; and that he has attended the following schools:

I therefore recommend that the said child be enrolled in this school. This 1st day of October, 1918 Alexander H. Kinnaird, M.D. School Physician, INDORSEMENT. A child showing one-sixteenth or less Indian blood, whose parents live on an Indian reservation, Indian fashion, who, if debarred from the Government schools, could not obtain an education, may be permitted in the reservation day and boarding schools, but it is preferable that it be not transferred to a nonreservation school, without special permission from the Office. Children showing one-eighth or less Indian blood, whose parents do not live on an Indian reservation, whose home is among white people where there are churches and schools, who are presumed to have adopted the white man's manners and customs, and are to all intents and purposes white people, are debarred from enrollment in the Government nonreservation and reservation schools. Superintendents, in all cases where doubt exists as to the degree of Indian blood of a child proposed for transfer, should fully satisfy themselves of the facts by affidavits from reliable persons, which affidavits must be kept on file at the school. A pupil who has been regularly enrolled in a nonreservation school must not be taken to any other nonreservation school without the consent of both Superintendents and the Commissioner of Indian Affairs, and Superintendents will be held to strict accountability for such pupils taken to their schools. A pupil dismissed from school for cause must not be enrolled in any other school without the permission of the Commissioner of Indian Affairs. Full facts must be submitted with each request. Southern Alaska Canning Company 503 CENTRAL BUILDING Seattle, Washington Quadra Cannery April 9th The Cushman School Tacoma. Attention to the Superintendent FOR FILE Dear Sir, Please find enclosed our check, $50.00 to cover the traveling expenses of Miss Lizzie Brown to Alaska. She is requested to return to Alaska as soon as possible by her Father, Joe Brown, as her help in the home is very much needed because her mother in the nearest future is going to have a baby. Hoping you will give this matter your best attention and see the girl off in a good party if possible, we beg to remain, Yours very truly, SOUTHERN ALASKA CANNING CO. This is written by request of me, Joe Brown Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., May 23, 1919 Mr. Joe Brown Quadra Bay, Alaska Dear Sir: Enclosed herewith find Vacation Request from Lizzie Brown. Please sign the request and return it to this office immediately, together with a deposit to defray all transportation expenses as per the requirements of the Vacation Request. Very respectfully, Superintendent. /MG Enc. Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Washington April 8, 1919. Mr. C. W. Waugh Box 212 Ketchikan, Alaska. Dear Sir: I beg to acknowledge receipt of your letter of March 23, 1919. The funds for Lizzie Brown have not yet been received but when Lizzie is ready to return home, I shall notify 503 Central Building, Seattle, Washington, so that they may meet her and provide transportation for her. I am very glad to report that Lizzie is in good health and appears to be happy and contented, as we strive to keep her. Very truly yours, Superintendent EHH:T REVILLA HOTEL CHAS. E. INGERSOLL, PROP. HARRY A. RICE, MGR. KETCHIKAN, ALASKA Cushman School Tacoma, Wn. 3/23/17 Dear Sir: Have instructed the Home office to send in your ear $50.00 for Lizzie Brown to be given her, when released from school. And before she leaves, please notify 503 Central Building Seattle, Wm. So that they may take care of her while at Seattle for transportation. Respectfully, S.W. Waugh Box 212, Ketchikan, Alaska. Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wash. Nov. 12, 1918. Mr. Jos. Brown, Care Southern Alaska Canning Co., Quedus, Alaska. Dear Mr. Brown: Mrs. Peterson of Seattle was in to see me last Saturday about your daughter and Frank Mark's daughter returning home. The girls had written her as they were homesick at first and later afraid of the epidemic of Spanish influenza. When Mrs. Peterson saw the girls, they had changed their minds again and told her they didn't want to go back until June. You should expect the children to become homesick but if you do not interfere with them, they soon recover and are happy. Lizzie and Selena were both sick with the grippe, but were out again in a few days. Don't worry about your daughter. She will be happier and more contented here with the many friends she has already made. Sincerely yours, Superintendent REQUISITION Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Washington 191 The following articles are needed in my department.

Smith Asst. clerk TO ALL MEMBERS OF THE CUSHION STUDENT ASSOCIATION Dear Friends: Nearly two years have passed since our last Reunion and Conference and I assure you it was with the keenest pleasure and expectation that I received word from Mr. Hammond, present Superintendent of Cushion, that I may again, in the name of the Association and of the School Faculty, invite you to the Seventh Annual Reunion and Conference of the Former Students of the Cushion School, to be held at the school June 17, 1918. The Reunion this year should be an event of unusual significance. The two years just past have seen many changes, both in the management and student body of the school. We should feel the necessity of our getting acquainted with the pupils and giving them the encouragement of our interests and support. We should get familiar with the advanced methods of the school that we may see at first hand the possibilities there are for the education of our children. We should keep in close touch with the school that our criticism may be always just and constructive; that our support may be genuine and effective. The program for the day includes three distinct features that we should come prepared to make the most of. Let us make the selection of our officers and the new organization of our Association a matter of first importance. Come prepared to take part in the afternoon conference and to say a word at the evening patriotic meeting. Let us put the best there is in us into the Association and work to make the Association an effective force in the education and uplift of our race. Make your presence in some way a contribution to the interest of your old school. I can assure you it will be a pleasure you will long remember. Very cordially yours, V. H. Johnson, President.
